summary: Kathleen D. Morrison is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She held an assistant professorship at Northwestern University (~1993–1995) and a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen Kenyon was an archaeologist who was educated at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College, Oxford. Her major career posts included the University of London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held academic posts at DePauw University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Lewis & Clark College (~1989–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

Kathleen M. Higgins is a philosopher who served as a resident scholar at the Bellagio Center (1993) and a visiting fellow at Australian National University (1997). She became a professor of philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin.

Kathleen McDonald is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Her education includes traditional study under Lama Thubten Yeshe (~1974–1984), as well as Tenzin Gyatso, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Kathryn H. Selig Brown is a scholar of Tibetology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan in 2000, where she studied under Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille is a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald. She held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and CRCAO, and edited EMSCAT.

Katragadda Paddayya is an archaeologist and Indologist who completed his doctorate at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1968. He was a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from approximately 1970 to 2008.

Indologist Katsuhiko Kamimura studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and at the University of Madras under V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University before serving as associate professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Doshisha University, he served as a professor at Hanazono University from approximately 1989 to 2016.

Katsuji Fujioka was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and Leipzig University (1901–1905). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1893 to 1896 and later held a post there from approximately 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki, an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and Hisashi Sato, and in Paris. He held assistant, associate, and full professor posts at Kyoto University between 1975 and 2010.

Katsumi Okimoto was a Buddhist studies scholar and sinologist who completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1973). He spent his career at Hanazono University as a professor (~1985–2009) and later as director (~2009–2020).

Katsumi Tanabe is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1968) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1990–1998) and Chuo University (~1998–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist who completed his degrees at Kyoto University. His career included posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University, Kansai University, Nara National Museum, and Ryukoku University.

Kavita Singh was an art historian and Indologist educated at Lady Shri Ram College, MSU Baroda, and Panjab University. She worked at the College of Art, Marg Publications, and became dean of the School of Arts and Aesthetics at JNU.

Kazi Dawa Samdup was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ugyen Gyatso and Lopen Tshampa Norbu. He served as headmaster at the Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and became a lecturer at the University of Calcutta in 1920.

Kazu Uehara was a historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyushu University. He worked as a lecturer at the University of Miyazaki and spent decades as an honorary professor at Seijo University from 1969 to 2017.
